newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee ends at 35.880/885, RBI buys dollars.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee ends at 35.880/885, RBI buys dollars.

text.p: The rupee ended a shade higher at 35.880/885 against the dollar on Thursday despite spot dollar purchases by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), dealers said.
The dollar opened the day at 35.89/90 against dollar.
Chinese paramount leader Deng Xiao Peng's death had no impact on the local forex market, dealers said.
"The Indian market is insulated from the rest of the world," said a dealer. "Even if something happens to President Clinton, the rupee will be unmoved."
The lowest level the rupee traded on Thursday was 35.8925, dealers said.
"Inward (dollar) remittances helped the rupee's rise," said a dealer. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) stepped in to arrest the rupee's rise, buying dollars upto 35.8850 level, he said.
The forwar dollar market was dull. The six month annualised premium closed at 6.97 percent, up from the previous close of 6.74 percent.
